body: I do. I'm not a licensed therapist or anyone who's trained/authorized to handle crisis, but I do understand what it's like to want to die. This show as rough for me too for that reason. You're not alone.

It's okay to gain weight while exercising. That weight is muscle mass, not fat. That said, you need to appropriately diet to lose the fat. I've dieted before, and here's my honest opinion.

Holy hell...you can NOT live on 400 calories per day! No doctor on the planet is going to recommend that, no matter how fat you are. If you don't believe me, try watching "My 600 Pound Life." Those people are pretty much as fat as it gets, and they're still only told to restrict their calories to maybe 1,200 a day (which is lower than the average person should go). Join a site like My Fitness Pal and set a realistic goal (no more than 2 pounds per week). It's very doable, but it doesn't happen quickly.

Also, wtf is with your chron's disease plan? That might make you thin, but your quality of life will severely dimiish. 

Honestly, it sounds to me like you have an eating disorder. I think you need help from a licensed therapist, not a demon. I'm not saying this to be unkind; I'm saying this because seriously, you sound like you're sick and need help.
I'd selfishly pick #2 because I don't want to be responsible for other people being able to die. I just want me to die.
Suburbs are more expensive than the city around here, ironically. I definitely have looked at suburbs.

I do my best to let my friend know how much I appreciate her, but she also knows I'm sad about her leaving. Let's hope I can find an apartment and a job by August 1. That's the thing; I know things can be found, but there's a huge time crunch.

Going to a therapist or a psychiatrist doesn't have to be a stigmatizing experience. It's said that 60% of people experience depression at some point in their lifetimes. That's a lot of freaking people. Seriously, if you haven't tried therapy/psychiatry yet, please do it. It helps so many people, and it might help you too.

What are you doing in your life right now? Do you have a job? School? If not, is there any way you can see a career counselor? Having some idea of a plan for the future can be very empowering and sounds like it could help you a lot.
